synopsis: The booklet distinguishes the deadliest documented collision pattern—a large machine moving over an unseen person or light vehicle—from the most frequently reported type, heavy-machine-to-heavy-machine contact, which usually causes property damage [f11293, f2977, f11440]. In the US haul-truck evidence for January 2005–June 2021, 54 deaths comprised 21 berm events, 13 collisions with people or vehicles, 12 dump-point events and eight other causes; 12 of the 13 collision deaths involved forward motion, and four began with victims within about 15 m [f2989, f2990, f2991]. This exposes a coverage mismatch: collision research emphasizes vehicle-to-vehicle interactions even though most haul-truck fatalities involve the environment [f395, f5935]. Australia's Model WHS regulation 215 requires collision risk control so far as reasonably practicable and a warning device, while the reviewed 2022 draft ISO 21815-3 requires sufficient CxS distance to stop before hitting an intended object [f2783, f2421]. Validation must address grade, non-longitudinal motion and braking timing—not merely detection or peak deceleration—and retain physical closed-loop tests near the collision/no-collision boundary [f6000, f6001, f6218, f7783, f10663, f7888]. Automatic stopping can itself cause rear-end collisions, tipping or load spill, shadow mode cannot establish those consequences, and no separate agency statistics were found for serious excavator swing collisions [f5814, f596, f11424].
